title: The Five-Fold Cosmos and Light Through the Gates
description: T97 argues that if even one of the five aspects of the natural mind were missing, the whole could not stand — whatever the proprium produces is at last swallowed in the great sea, because nothing the soul claims can stand on its own. The Lord makes five things known to the rational: that it belongs to the kind of the light, that the degrees of formation and of darkness exist in a certain manner, that the light puts the proprium's claim to shame and prevails, that the soul has come to the boundary of death and is brought out by the upper gate, that the proprium is bound at last with a great bond. T98 describes how the Lord's truth comes forth through the open gates of the rational's discrete degrees: rays extending along fitted channels, four gates open at every quarter and downward into dwelling-places, drawing what is the Lord's by the hand from the lowest places and bearing it upward — passing through the orders without breaking them.
